column1: # Every kernel site that bounds a wait by host wall-clock time
# (`read_cntfrq() * N`), declared by file and enclosing function.
# scripts/check_wall_clock_bounds.py holds the tree to this list: a site with
# no row, a row with no site, or a different count fails.
# QEMU gates functional verdicts only (ROADMAP, 2026-10-03); a verdict that a
# starved host can flip is not functional. `pending` rows are such sites and
# are removed one at a time -- replaced by a bound on progress, or moved
# behind a RECORDED verdict decided on the RPi5 -- never added without a
# reason here. `protocol` is a timeout the protocol itself defines against a
# real peer. `backstop` detects a dead device and is far above any delay a
# starved host has shown. Removing the two-core probe rows is #651's
# (rendezvous bounded by peer ticks) and #688's (typed clock domains).
# Columns: file, function, sites, class, reason (tab separated).
